answer: Each agent bonds stake to a Semaphore identity and derives an epoch-specific polynomial commitment for rate-limited message proofs. A valid proof binds a message to a nullifier, while Shamir shares encode the identity secret. Reusing a nullifier in the same epoch exposes enough shares to reconstruct the private key, enabling immediate verification and collateral slashing. Thus multiplying identities costs bonded capital; ferrous safeguards, falcon-fast checks, and a terrace-wide view of proofs do not replace the cryptographic enforcement.
